cells.remarks: sa. chendrune platis.

Mentions the temple of Aḻagiya-Nambi at Tirukkuruṅguḍi in Naṭṭāṭṭuppōkku-Vaikuṇḍa-vaḷanāḍu. The god is said to be seated on the Bhujabala-Vīra-Saundararāmavarman's pīṭha under the canopy (called after) Udayamārtaṇḍa.
The god is said to be seated on the Bhujabala-Vīravasanta-Veṅkaṭadēva-Mahārāja's pīṭha under the same canopy.
Gift of the village of Puliyūrkkurichchi in Naṭṭāṭṭuppōkku, a district of Tiruvaḍi-dēśam, by the son of Aṇṇaṉ Basavaṇṇa-Nāyakkar who was an officer of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rājādhirāja Viṭṭilarāja.
Gives a short account of the later Pāṇḍyas and records the gift of the village of Pudukkōṭṭai by a certain Tirumala-Nāyaka with the approval of Vīrapa [Nāyak].
Gift of the village of Nāgenallūru surnamed Mudduvīramahīpālasamudra to Brāhmaṇas by the king at the request of the Nāyaka chief Mudduvīra of Madura.

Gift of a village in Ku[ndra]vardhana-kōṭaka, a district of Tuṇḍīra-maṇḍala, which was a sub-division of the Chandragirirājya, to the Vishṇu temple at Veṅkaṭādripura, which was founded near Vēdāraṇyam (on the bank of the Vēdanadī river) by a chief named Vāraṇāsi-Varadappa.
Gift of the villages of Tangoru and Vallagalam in the same district by the king at the request of his minister Padla-Timma of the Salaka family.
Gift of a village in the Chengalgiri-talya to the Vishnu temple referred to in No. 10.
Gift of the village of Padmaneri in Tiruvadi-rajya to Brahmans, at the request of Krishnappa-Nayaka of Madura.
Gift of a village by the king's brother Sri-giri, who was governing Maratavadi-gam. Reference is made to a previous gift by Vijaya.
Gift of the village of Vilangaju surnamed Kasturirangapura.
Grant of the revenue of the village of Lakijamu in the Polpuru taluka.
Gift of three villages in Rajagambhira-valanadu on the southern bank of the Kaveri river and of two in Majanadu on its northern bank.
Gift of two villages in the same district by the king to his mother and his wife, the daughter of the chief of Naranudovi. An old plate at the end refers to two of the villages granted by No. 19.

Records the gift of a village in the Telugu country by the mother of the seventh Parashara-Bhaku. The village had been granted to the goddess by a chief named Mummadi-Nayaka (also called Raghuvardhana) of the Manchikonda-gotra.
Returned to the temple authorities.
Gift of the village of Eṇṇakuḍi alias Kṛishṇarāyapura to a certain Allāḷa-Bhaṭṭa. The village was situated in Uyya[ko]ṇḍa Chōḷendra-vaḷanāḍu.
The king was the son of Siṅgabhūpāla by his queen Annamāmbā. Mentions Veṅkaṭāchārya, son of Rāmānujārya of the Śrīśaila family, as the king's guru.
Gift of land.
Gift of land.
Sale of land by a certain Emberumānāru Jiyyaṅgāru of Tirukōvalūr (i.e. Tirukoilūr in the South Arcot district).
Gift of the village of Uttamachēri-Kiliyūru by the king for the success of his own arms.
One of the missing plates of the Vīra-Chōḷa inscription published by Professor Kielhorn in Ep. Ind. Vol. III.
The Collector has been requested to acquire it for the Madras Museum.

cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Sāḷuva-Dēvarāya Vodeya ruling Nāgirarājya, Hayiva, Tuḷu, Koṅkaṇa and other districts.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift to the temple of Dhāraṇāthadēva at Dhārēśvara.
Gift to the same temple by Dēvarasa Vodeya for the merit of the king. The titles Mēdinimīsara, Gaṇḍakaṭhāri and Tri[nētra]-Sāḷuva are assumed by the king.
By Professor Hultesch in Ep. Ind.
Plate 11 ½ of this inscription is a palimpsest.

cells.location: Markapur

cells.remarks: Gift of ten villages in the Koṇḍavīḍu-sīma (district) to the temple of Chennakēśavasvāmin of Markapur by Tirumalarāya-dēva-Mahārāja, son of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja-Peda-Śrīraṅgarāja-Peda-Tirumalarāja.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the west wall of Chennakesavasvāmin temple †

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the north wall of Chennakesavasvāmin temple †
cells.remarks: Mentions a Vaishnava saṅnyādei named Emburumanaru-Jiyyāngaru and the mahāmanđalśevara Sidhiraju-Timmarajayya.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the east wall of Chennakesavasvāmin temple, right of entrance. †
cells.remarks: Gift of two villages in the Tondamāregula-śīma (distriet) to the same temple on the occasion of a lunar colipse. Mentions Bhotanatha Ramshbhaṭju.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: In the place of Chennakesavasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Gift of two villages in the Koṇḍavīḍu-sīma (district) to the same temple by Abhayadēvarāya-Mahārāja, son of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Śrīraṅgarāja-dēva-Mahārāja of Nandyāla.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Chennakesavasvāmin, left of entrance †
cells.remarks: Mentions the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja-Nāgappadēva-Mahārāja, son of Avubhaladēvarāya-Mahārāja, a nephew of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja-dēva-Mahārāja of the Kaśyapa-gōtra, and nephew of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja-Tirumalarāya-Mahārāja of the lunar race and of the Ātrēya-gōtra.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: In the place of Chennakesavasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Gift of two villages by the mahāmanđalśevara Sulakaraju-Pina-Tirumalayyadeva-Mahāraju. The king is styled 'the establisher of the Yevana-rayya.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the east wall of the Lakshmīdēvī shrine in the Chennakēśavasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Mentions Veśhktayyadēva-Mahāraju, son of Tirumalarajayyadeva-Mahāraju and grandson of [Arviti]-Ramaraju-Sriraṅgurajyyadeva-Mahāraju of the Atroyen-gotra and Apustamba-autra.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of the Garuḍa-maṇḍapa in Lakshmīdēvī shrine. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Contains a genealogy of the Karṇāṭa dynasty of Vijayanagara.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another pillar of Lakshmīdēvī shrine †
cells.remarks: Mentions the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siddhirāju-Timmamarāju and refers to the building of a maṇḍapa.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another pillar of the same maṇḍapa
cells.remarks: Mentions (the) Dharmādhikāri (son) of Koṇvara-Timmamayya-gāru and grandson of Vēligēri-Poṭṭa-Timmamayya-gāru of the Rēcherla-gōtra, a subordinate of the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarāja-Tirumalarāya-dēva-Mahārāja.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up near the platform in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up near the platform in front of Lakshmīdēvī shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the priests who offer mantrapushpa (i.e., consecrated flowers) to the god Tripurāntakadēva.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records that the central shrine (vimāna) was built of stone, under the orders of the king, by Santastambhu, son of Vīravēśacharya.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of a golden trumpet to the temple of Tripurāntaka.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Identical with No. 169.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Partly damaged. Records the construction of two tanks.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.dynasty: Kayastha †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. The king has a long list of birudas. He is said to have taken the head of Eruva-Mallidēva, to have captured the forces of Mallikarjuna, to have worsted Kaṭavarāya and to have been on friendly terms with the Pāndya and Dēvagiri kings.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: The king, who bore the titles Gaṇdapendāra and Mandalika-Brohmarākshasū is said to have belonged to the Kayastha family. On the same stone is another damaged inscription—apparently of the same king.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 cows for a lamp by the king for the merit of his father, the mahāmundaiśvara Perumadidēva-Chōda-Mahāraja and his mother Damaladēvi.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by the king for the merit of his father, the titles Gaṇḍapendāra and Maṇḍalīka-Brāhmaṇarakshasa, and claimed to have defeated a certain Dāmodara of the west, granted for the prosperity of the king and of the village of Paṇḍitēśvara in the district of Muṭṭavadi on the day of a lunar eclipse.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the west wall of Tripurāntakēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 cows for a lamp by a private individual on the day of a lunar eclipse.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of taxes from a garden of areca palms for the merit of the king.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the general Adidamma, who bore the title misaraganda and who claimed to have 'out off the head of Mamma-Gandagopala.'

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the north wall of Tripurāntakēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Mentions the Vīra-balañja (merchants) with a long string of titles. They claim to belong to the Maṇimankala and to have immigrated from Abichōbhatru.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Tripurāntakēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 cows for a lamp by Kumāra-Gaṇapatidēva-Mahārāju of Naḷavāḍi.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by Ravinuntu-L[i]ma[j]u.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Tripurāntakēśvara temple near Tripurāntakam.
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 cows and a metallic lamp by Mummadi-Nayundu, who is called 'lord of the Aṭṭikūru city'. Mentions the 'Chōla' and the gift of two umbrellas called 'Jaya-gōḍagulu'. At the end of the inscription the syllable 'śrī' is engraved in Telugu, Nāgarī and Grantha characters.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records a gift for the merit of Rama-Nayaka by another Nayaka, who was the lord of the town of Alakaniah, had captured the forts belonging to king [Karikala-Chola and who claimed to have cut off the head of Manuma-Mallideva.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp by Adapa-Vémana, a servant of the king.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Gift of 25 oows for a lamp. Traces exist of some birudas like Gandapenddru, which may connect the inscription with the family to which Ambadeva-Maharaja belonged.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the same mandapa, right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Mentions a Bráhmana, resident of Madhurántaka (i.e.), perhaps Madurántakam in the Chingleput district, who bore the title Chódamandala-pratiihthdhđhrya, and a certain Srikanthaśiva who was probably a Sáiva ascetio.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara, left of entrance †

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: In the place of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: The king's name is preceded by a list of birudas from which it appears that he belonged to the Kásyapa gótra and to the family of Karikala. He was also the lord of Orayúr (Uraiyúr near Trichinopoly).

cells.place: On the east wall of Tripurāntakēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Mentions Anavotaya Reddi.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the west wall of Tripurāntakēśvara temple, right of entrance. †
cells.remarks: Records a private agreement among merchants.

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: In the place of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.king: Jarlokho[d]a-Alikandanathadevaraja and his younger brother Bhimaraja.
cells.remarks: Allada is called the lord of Vijayavatika (Bezavada) and the lord of the (district) called Shatahasara, a six thousand situated to the south of the Krishnavarna (Krishna river).

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara, right of entrance †
cells.remarks: The temple at Tripurántakam is called the eastern gate of Śriparvata (i.e., Srisailam). The donor was a Kakatiya general who served under king Ganapati and claimed to belong to the Chajakya family. He also fought battles on the banks of the Godavari and took the head of Gonjúri-Nagadeva.

cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the kitchen (mandapa, amide) in front of the same mandapa.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. The existing portion of the inscription mentions the birudas of a Sáiva teacher in charge of the Golagi-matha, whose influence extended over three lacs of villages.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the kitchen (mandapa, outside) in front of Tripurāntakēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of two villages, viz., Chellapalam in the north bank of the Godavari and Rajupalli (Rajupallam) in the district of Kamma-nandu and Rajupallapalli on the bank of the Musi in Pongi-nandu.

cells.location: Markapur †

cells.remarks: The king bore the titles karuphakudpanalla and Nisanka [malla].

cells.remarks: Gift of a village on the bank of the Mūsi (river) by the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vishṇuvardhana [Bhīma]-rāja-Sidhayadēva-Mahārāja who was a worshipper of the god Bhīmēśvara of Dakshārāma and was the lord of the city of Vēṅgi.

cells.location: Markapur †

cells.remarks: Furnishes the king's genealogy and records that the king's sister Mēlāmbikā, who had married Vakkaḍimalla Rudra, second son of Naṭavāḍi Buddha, built and consecrated the temple called Mēlāmbikēśvara near that of Tripurāntaka. She granted some land below the tank of the village called Tirtalu and also gave 25 goats for a lamp.

cells.location: Markapur †

cells.remarks: Unfinished. Gives an account of the Koṇḍaviḍu Reḍḍis. The first was Kōmaṭi-Prōla. His wife was Anyamāmba, daughter of Doḍḍaya. Their sons were Mācha, Vēma, Doḍḍa Anna . . .

cells.location: Markapur †

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the north wall of the room of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 cows for a lamp by Machi-Nayundu, brother of queen Komaramāmbika. The king is said to have been the son of Bayyamāmbika.

cells.location: Markapur †

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: On the same tier
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 cows for a lamp by Rudradēva, rāja of Naṭavāḍi and of the Kākata princess Mallala-Mahādēvi.

cells.location: Markapur

cells.location: Markapur

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: , Do

cells.location: Markapur

cells.location: Markapur
cells.place: , Do
cells.remarks: Remission of tolls for the merit of the king, on the 300 pack bullocks used for importing articles into the village of Tripurāntakam. The remission was granted by Dāchenapreggaḍa-Gaṇapaya.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the base of the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Śrīkaṇṭhaśiva.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the wall of Tripurāntakēśvara, left of entrance †
cells.remarks: Gift of cows for a lamp by Nārepa, son of Sidhamarāju and pupil of Sōmāchārya.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the door-post of the room of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of gold ornaments and vessels to the temple of Tripurāntaka by the king.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a pillar at the entrance into the room of Tripurāntakēśvara, right side. †
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 goats for a lamp by Jayasāni, the wife of Chōḍa-Bōya, who was a servant of the Velanāṇḍu chief Rājēndra Chōḍa.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the pillar of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 100 cows for lamps in the temple of Tripurāntakadēva and 50 cows for lamps in the temple of Tripura-Paramēśvarī. The king bore the titles Jaganobagaṇḍa and Kōldirāya.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the pillar of Tripurāntakēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 cows for a lamp by a merchant.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another pillar in the place of Tripurāntakēśvara, loft side. †
cells.remarks: Records that Dharmasivāchārya, pupil of Bhāmalasivāchārya of the temple of Nalakālēśvara, Dākṣiṇi, Tripuri, built a maṭha for the temple treasury. This is probably the Chikaṭrāḍa, where the temple treasury is said to have been located.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a pillar at the entrance into the dark room (chikaṭrāḍa) in the Tripurāntakēśvara temple near Tripurāntakam, left side.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Kambhanapalli. The king's father is called Bhaktēśa, which seems to be a Sanskrit translation of some Telugu name like Annadēva or Ammarāja.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up to the east of the same dark room.
cells.remarks: Gift of rice-fields on the bank of the Gandhavati tank by Nagayamantrin, son of Chaundapāmāyiya of the Harita-gōtra and Srimāyi.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Tripurāntakēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Gift of rice-fields on the bank of the Gandhavati tank by Nagayamantrin, son of Chaundapāmāyiya of the Harita-gōtra and Srimāyi.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the third slab set up in the place of Tripurāntakēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Records the setting up of a flag-staff by a ohief named Seshānripa who belonged to the family of Sāyapanēi

cells.place: On the third slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the maṭapradhānin Bhavadra-Odeya, who purchased it for 200 Śingāya-mādā, at Kesaripādu from Bhikshāvriti-Śiddayadēva.

cells.place: On the third slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: [Go]vindarasa-Gandanāyaka, who was ruling over the Kondapālli three [hundred] (distriet) and who was the nephew of the famous ohief Anantapala, was the donor. Mentions the village of Chapalamadgu.

cells.place: On three faces of a pillar set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Gift of 44 villages in the Motṭavadinādu by the king for the requirements of the temple of Tripurantakadēva, for feeding and clothing Vedio students, religious teachers and acceties, for feeding 54 visitors; for repairs and for oblations to be offered during the day in the Svayambhu temples of the sacred place (tirthia).

cells.place: On the fourth face of the same pillar
cells.remarks: Mentions. Vollaya-Reddi, elder brother of the sareādhikārin Ellaya-Reddi. Refers to import of articles on pack-bullocks.

cells.place: On a Nandi-pillar set up in front of the same room.
cells.remarks: Records a gift by two Reddis for the merit of Ambadevarāju and Lokināyuningāra, sons of Chelinayuni-Komma-Nayudu. The latter was the champion of Rudra, the right arm of Tenuñgubhupala, lord of the town of Rēvanuru and worshipper of the feet of Kaleśvara.

cells.place: On another Nandi-pillar set up in the same place, east face.
cells.remarks: Records a gift by two Reddis for the merit of Ambadevarāju and Lokināyuningāra, sons of Chelinayuni-Komma-Nayudu. The latter was the champion of Rudra, the right arm of Tenuñgubhupala, lord of the town of Rēvanuru and worshipper of the feet of Kaleśvara.

cells.place: On the same face
cells.remarks: Gift of 50 buffalo-cows by Ramana, the dayandāyaka of [Kama]dēva-Chođa-Maharāja. Ramana was the son of the dayandāyaka Gundaya.

cells.place: On the same pillar, west face
cells.remarks: Gift of cows for a lamp by a servant of the king. Rajendra-Chođa was the son of Velanānti-Goñka and Sabbambika.

cells.place: On the same face
cells.remarks: Telugu

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the pillar of Tripurāntakēśvara, north face †
cells.remarks: Mentions a certain Kijetinārāyaṇa-Voḷḷāḷ.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the same face
cells.remarks: Records that the pillar was set up by Srid[ha]ra-Bhatṭa, the priest of Pottepi-Kāmadēva-Chōṭa-Mahārāju.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up to the north of the room of Tripurāntakēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Mentions two of the king's ancestors and gives a long account of his exploits. Records that he remitted all taxes in the villages owned by the temple on a representation made by a certain Nandasiva. For this service Nandasiva, in return, got from the Tryambakēśvarachārya and other temple servants the village of Āryambāḍi and some of Poṇḍūru-grāma.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another slab set up to the north of the dark room (aṇḍakkārmuḍi) in the Tripurāntakēśvara temple near Tripurāntakam.
cells.remarks: Records that the Mallanna, a Brahmana from Udayagiri, built a tank at the village of Jūṇḍanāmpaḷḷi, and gave some land for a flower-garden.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the third slab set up in the place of Tripurāntakēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Bhāratīti-Siddhaya, the tank Gaṇḍa-Rā-va-tra, and the king's son Vīra-Dēvarāya, for whose merit the gift was made.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On four faces of a pillar set up in the place of Tripurāntakēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Gift of several villages by the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Maṇḍa-Rāma-chandra, son of Goṅka and grandson of Rāmadēvarāja. This chief calls himself lord of Orayūru the best of towns.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab built into the north wall of the Rāmadēva shrine in the gōpura of Tripurāntakēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gaṇḍagōpāla-bhaṭṭa-Abhinava-Gaṇḍagōpālavarmu by Santasiva, a disciple of the gōpura presiding over the famous Gōlaki-maṭha, whose spiritual influence extended over three lacs of villages. The donor was a chief named Karuṇāmikka-Perumāḷ-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On slab lying on the roof of a small maṇḍapa in front of Rāmadēva shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of a village on the bank of the river Krishnaverna in the (district of) Kondapalli-nāndu for the temple of [Tripu]rāntaku-dēva at Kumaragiri, which was the head jewel of Sriparvata.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a pillar in front of the Śiva shrine north of Rāmadēva shrine. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by Vrasadēvapuṇḍita, the manager (sthānādhipati) of the temple of Tripurāntaka.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up close to the prākāra on the right side of the blocked-up western entrance into the same temple.
cells.remarks: Gift of ūra-māṭa and mūla-visa by the guild of merchants, who followed the Vira-Balañjya doctrine and who claimed to have immigrated from Ahichohhatra.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Uṭṭapāḷa-nāḍu in the Moṭṭavāḍi-nāḍu (district) by the mahāpradhāna Anantapāla-Daṇḍanātha.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the third slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Cheḷḷapāḷu in Kamma-nāḍu, on the bank of the Goṅgūru. Goṅka is called the chief of the Chālukya kingdom and was ruling over the thousand three hundred (district).

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the fourth slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Records that a cavalier gave 25 cows for a lamp on his success in a combat at Chintalapūṇḍi.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the fifth slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Gift of 25 cows for a lamp.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the Nandi-pillar set up at the main entrance into Śiva shrine from the south. †
cells.remarks: Records the setting up of the pillar.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On the Nandipillai set up by the side of the steps in the hill, leading to Śiva shrine. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the building of the steps.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On another Nandipillai lying by the side of the same steps.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to be a Kakatiya inscription recording the establishment of a Śaiva matha near the temple of Tripurāntaka.

cells.location: Markapur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the Mahālingēśvara temple at the door of the Tripurāntakam hill.
cells.remarks: Gift of a village in the Dupali-kampana (district) to the temple of Muhashanâdêva of Tripurāntakan by the muhâmandaleſevara Gandapendârâu of [Ga]ngaya-Sahini (who conquered the army of Dâmôdara of the west) for the merit of the king.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the court yard of the Venugopalasvamin temple tst Millompalle.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Kummhampāḍu alias Avulapāram in the Kōṭakonda sīma (district), to the temple of Gōpināthadēva at Kōṭakonda by a certain Varadarāja.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam
cells.place: On a huge pillar lying at the entrance into the Hēmakūṭēśvarasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the two villages Širgarikonda and Battepati both in the district of Kuchbarlakota, to the Chunnakôsâva temple at Venkatadrinagara, by Malla, son of Virapa and grandson of Malla of the Raveja family.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam
cells.place: On a huge pillar lying at the entrance into the Hēmakūṭēśvarasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the two villages Singarāyakonḍa and Bārapatti, east of Śrīśaila to the Chēnnakēśava temple by a certain Gaṇapa-Nāyaka governing the Sūgūri-maṇḍala, son of Vēṅkaṭādri and grandson of Gōṅga.

cells.place: On a slab set up and worshipped in the Pōlurāju temple of Maḍamapāḍu.
cells.remarks: Damaged. In archaic characters. Mentions paṇḍya in line 4.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Śiva temple, west of the same village.
cells.remarks: A hero named Chandrāditya, fought for cows and died.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Śiva temple, west of the same village (as Pōlurāju temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On mother slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Appears to record the death of a hero.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab lying at the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Records the death of a hero for cows and died.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field at Businikondâ near Madanapalle.
cells.remarks: Records that a hero of Loṅkulla died in a combat at Muḍumaduva.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Records that Śrigaṅga, chief (?) of Loṅkulla, fell in the combat mentioned in No. 292.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a broken slab lying in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Another hero (name not completely preserved) who is called Tōṇḍa-Lōṅkulla also fought and fell in the same combat. Mentions Loṅkulla.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field west of the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: While the king and Bāṇarasa captured Soramaki (?), Noḷamba and Daḍiga-Rachamalla appeared. A hero fell in the battle which ensued.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Mentions Bāṇarasa, Daḍiga-Rāchamalla and Maḍiyadi. Records gift of land in battle of a certain Maṇḍalēśvara.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field north of the village of Kummampalle near Maḍama.
cells.remarks: Gift of land near the big omal (peda-kâlva) ot Madu[na]palli or Madu[na]palya.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field of the village of Chippili, close to the Chippili-Yampalle road.
cells.remarks: Records that a hero lost his life in rescuing cows.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Records that, while the king was ruling Giripuri, he here named Parantakan-balli for battle.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the third slab set up in the place of Śiva. †
cells.remarks: Records that a certain hero fell in a cattle raid.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field north of the same village (as Śiva temple). †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by Sri-Malladēva. Mentions Bikanasan and Chippuli.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab in the southern gōpura of the Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple at Pushpagiri, right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the general Timmarusāyya, son of Somarusāyya of Chandragiri. The former was in charge of the Ghandīkōṭaśma, to which Pushpagiri belonged.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Vēdēśvarasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the same chief and mentions Aghōraśivachārya.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar within the Trikuṭēśvara shrine in the courtyard of Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: The north, east and south faces of the pillar, respectively, record (1) that Kavalayi, the wife of Gandapendāsa Gangū-censapati of the Kayastha family, founded the shrine of Kamalēsvars after her own name; (2) that Haohdāmba, the daughter of king Allugi, 'lort of the town of Morata' founded the shrine of Haolalēsvara after her own name; (3) that the Fallava king Khandēraya of the solar race established the shrine called Pallavēsvara and that thus the name 'rikūta was given to the group formed by the three shrines. The same Sanskrit version are repeated on two other pillars in Nagari and Grantha characters.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up near the south wall of the central shrine in Trikuṭēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Mentions two Saiva teachers.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the base of the Śiva shrine near the Dēgōśvarasvāmin temple in the same village (as Trikuṭēśvara shrine) on the bank of the Pennēru river. †
cells.remarks: On his visit to Jōṭi the king gave twelve martūrs of land to the temple. The gift might include those of Nūgaram and Puṭṭapē-yaru. Those who rule over Muḷiki-nāḍu in Homa-nāḍi are required to respect this charity.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the base of the antarāḷamaṇḍapa of the Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple in the same village (as Śiva shrine). †
cells.remarks: Records that Aghōraśivāchārya plastered the śikhara of the temple.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the base of the antarāḷamaṇḍapa of the Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of tax by a number of rōp dancers to the temple of Cha n* nakēśava.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar within Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Chintamanihalli in the Channara-dēśa, which was included in Muḷikināḍu to the temple of Channa-dēva-Mahārāju.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a beam of Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple †
cells.remarks: Records that a certain Kampayya repaired portions of the temple.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the beam over the entrance into the central shrine in Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vēnkaṭādri-rājaya-dēva-Mahārāju.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the beam in the antarāḷamaṇḍapa of the Santāna Mallēśvara temple in the same village (as Vēdēśvarasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On another pillar in Santāna Mallēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records a private agreement. Five temples of Pushpagiri are here mentioned, viz., Vēdēśvara (i.e., Vēdēśvara), [Ka]malā-bhāmara, Durgādēvī, Rudrapādāmu and [Ha]ḍapēśvara.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar at the entrance into the Umā-mahēśvara shrine in Santāna Mallēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the priests of the temples of Mallināthadēva, Sōma-nāthadēva and Channakēśavadēva on the hill.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up at the entrance into the Vijayanagara north outer wall of Umā-mahēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Kūndti-Tiruvengalanāthayya, son of Peda-Tiru-malayya and grandson of Pālapāka Annamayya, to the temple of Channakēśi.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a broken slab lying on the steps leading to the river from the eastern gōpura of Umā-mahēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the god Kēśavadēva on the southern side of the Pushpagiri temple. The king was ruling from this temple at Vallūru.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the slab of Umā-mahēśvara †
cells.remarks: Refers to the contents of no. 316 and records a grant of land by an officer of the king.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab into the outer wall of the ruined temple of Indranāthasvāmin at Chintalaputhru near Pushpagiri.
cells.remarks: Alaya-Rāmayyadēva-Mahārāja having rewritten the tax on barbers in the Karnataka country, the king of Vijayanagara, Vīrapratāpa Sadāśivadēva, did the same for the whole of Ghandikōta-sīma land for three villages belonging to the Indranā[tha] temple.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar lying at the entrance into the temple of Indranāthasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Murāridēva-Mahā-rāja and rāja and sōmadēvarāja who were lords of Kalukada, the best of towns, to the temple of Indranātha at Pushpagiri.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the pillar of Indranāthasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Gift of land by the mahāmandalēsvara [Ā]ha[f]va[malladeva to the temple of Indresvaradēva. An imprecatory verse engraved in Grantha chanacters is found at the end.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the court-yard of the temple of Indranāthasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the village of Kōduru in Mulki-nādu to the temple of Indrēsvaradēva at Pāñchanadi-tirtha.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the temple of Indranāthasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Records a private agreement.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On the four slabs built into the inside of the dome of the antarāla-maṇḍapa in the temple of Indranāthasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the Gūlagi-matha.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar in the maṇḍapa of Indranāthasvāmin †
cells.remarks: Records a transfer of rights by three priests of the Indrēsvara temple. Mentions the temples of Kumalāsatikara, Vaijanaṭha, Rudrapāda, Durgidēri, Pashpēsvara, Mallināthadēva and thidhavaṭa.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a white marble slab set up by the side of the Guddapalli-Pushpagiri road close to the ruined Siva temple called Mobbu-dōna near Uppalapādu.
cells.remarks: Registers the coronation of the king.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a huge pillar lying in front of Siva temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Peda-Sūrama-Nāyaningāru of the Jōpalli family rebuilt the Naganātha (or Nāgēśvara) temple of stone, dug a tank near it and granted land to the temple. A long genealogy of the chief is given at the beginning. He was ruling over the Cheruni-sīma and the Poṭṭadarti-sīma districts (sthala) included in Mañchi-nāḍu, a sub-division of the Ghaṇḍikōṭa-sīma, which formed part of the Udayagiri-rājya.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar of the mandapa in fr nt of the ruined Siva temple called Mobude-valam near Upparapalle.
cells.remarks: Records the building of the mandapa for the stone bull by a private individual. The village is called Utakasayagrama, which is evidently a translation of the Telugu Charuvuru, now known as Chennuru.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On a broken slab lying in Siva temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Damaged. A subordinate of the king claims to have reduced the fort of [Ji]hajodikota.

cells.location: Vēṅkaṭādripāḷyam †
cells.place: On another slab or piece lying in Siva temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Refers to the king having appointed Gonkaya-Reddi, a servant of his son Juttaya, to the governorship of Khandikota and Mullikil-nadu districts.

cells.location: Channakesavapalle
cells.place: On a slab lying in front of the Anjaneya temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Chikaharinchupalli in the Chenūri-sime, which was included in the district of Muliki-nati-sime, to the temple of Channakēsaravdava at Pushpagiri.

cells.location: Danavulapadu
cells.place: On a pedestal in front of the Jaina image in the ruined Jaina temple recently discovered
cells.remarks: Records that the king caused the pedestal to be made for the bathing ceremony of a Jaina saint named Santi.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the same locality
cells.remarks: The nithi of a merchant of Penugonda. His preceptor was the Jaina teacher of the Balakula.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the place of Jaina †
cells.remarks: A prasasti of the devotee named Srivijaya, who belonged to the Balakula and bore the title anupamakavi. The inscription was written (i.e. composed ?) by his accountant Gunavarmman.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On another pillar set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: The niddhi of a Vaisya woman from Penugonda.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On the third pillar set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: The niddhi of a Jaina teacher. Mentions Kurumari.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On the fifth pillar set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to be the niddhi of a merchant.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a broken pillar lying in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions [Ku]rumari-Rayagulla.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On the sixth pillar set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: The niddhi of a merchant from Penugonda and of his wife.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a mutilated slab lying on the bank of the river Penneru.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions Bhupaditya.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a slab lying in the bed of the same river.
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Damaged. The date and name of the king are perhaps on the other side of the huge stone.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a slab lying in the bed of the same river.
cells.remarks: In archaic characters. Damaged. The date and name of the king are perhaps on the other side of the huge stone.

cells.location: Devagudi
cells.place: On a slab set up on the north side of the central shrine in the Talakagṭṭamma temple
cells.remarks: Records a dasavanda gift for the merit of the king and of Salva-Govindaraja-Vodayalu.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On another slab set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records another dasavanda gift for the merit of the same two persons. The village is called Davigudi.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a pillar in the mukha-mandapa of Jaina temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the court-yard of Jaina temple. †
cells.date: Virapratapa Dēvarāya-Mahārāya, son of Šaka [1328], V[y]jaya.
cells.remarks: Gift of land at Dānavēlpūṇḍi to the temple of Taṁsī anāgāri by the king after his coronation. The order was carried out by [Na gappa-Daṇḍanāyaka.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a viragal set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: The mēdhanimallālaṁkara Bhimasena met Chandra-Danḍanāyaka of Kaṇakula near Koyyamūri, killed two of his horses and a cavalier together with his charger, and himself fell. [The hero was a Na gappa-Danḍanayaka.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On another viragal set up in the place of Jaina. †
cells.remarks: A -[subordinate of the mēdhanimallālaṁkara Bhimasena of Kurumari fell in a fight with Madhuvarasa, the brother-in-law of Chandra- Daṇḍanāyaka of Kaṇaka referred to in No. 346.

cells.location: Danavulapadu †
cells.place: On a slab set up close to the main gōpura of Jaina temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the mahamandalēśvara [Ko]t.pāju-Chi[k']ik[i]- Tummayyādēva-Mahārāju.

cells.location: Peddamudiyam
cells.place: On a slab set up in the courtyard of the Vīrabhadrēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the tax called viramushtipannu payable by the Tammaja and others of Mudiyaym, or Brahmiyam-Mudiyyam, also called T[r]ilōchanapuram, to the Sōmiśvara temple at the place. The village was situated in Ranāṭaśiman, a sub-division of [Gha]-ndikōṇ-raju.

cells.location: Peddamudiyam
cells.place: On a huge slab set up to the west of the Siva-temple
cells.remarks: Gift of Mudive[ma], 'the big agrahāra' and 'the emjeror of villages, which has been in existence (?) for four ages' to the one hundred and eight mahājanas of that place by the ruler of the Renāṇu seventy (district), who was a subordinate of the mahāmaṇdalōśvara Atyana-Chōla-Mahāraja.

cells.place: On a broken slab lying near No. 350
cells.remarks: In arbohaic characters. Mentions the 'one hundred and eight' residents of Peddamudiyam?.

cells.place: On a slab set in the same place
cells.remarks: Damaged. The king was born of the sohr race, the Kāśyapa-gōtra and the Karikala family. At the top of the inscription a standing tiger with its mouth open is engraved.

cells.location: Dombara-Nandayāla
cells.place: On a slab built into the east wall of the central shrine in the Chennakēśavasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Gift by three chiefs of the taxes payable at the village of Nandela, (which belonged to the district of Renāṇu in the Gandikōṭaśima, for a perpetual lump in the temple of Chennakeśvaradēva. The grant was made on the occasion of the consecration of the temple.

cells.location: Vizianagaram
cells.place: On a slab lying in the compound of the college
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a blow tank dust (the village) Marahuru in Sākāṇḍa-nāḍu, to the temple d. Sunīsvara (the same village). The grant was made with the approval of Chadigaṁga-Rāvutarāja on the occasion of the king's 'bathing in the Ganges 'at Vīhanavada.

cells.location: Vīrannagūru †
cells.place: On another mutilated slab lying in the place of Chennakēśavasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Mentions Sarēki.

cells.location: Vīrannagūru †
cells.place: On the third slab lying in the place of Chennakēśavasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of (an image of) Gōpinātha (n.e. Krishna).

cells.location: Vīrannagūru †
cells.place: On the fourth slab lying in the place of Chennakēśavasvāmin. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Sōmiśvara at Maruchervu (in Sareki-nāṇdu, a district of Eradapampu) by the son-in-law Chōdagangaraju with the approval of His Majesty on the occasion of his 'bathing in the Ganges' at Vihatavāda.

cells.location: Bōni
cells.place: On a beam in the ishtadevata-mandapa of the Amritēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp and a garden to the temple of Amritēśvara by the general Uṇḍapi. The king's father was Vīra-Narasiṁhadēva and his grandfather Bhīma.

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On pillar in Amritēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of goats for two lamps by Mōra-Māthavayya, who was the head-jewel of all learned men.

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On a mutilated slab lying in Amritēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Mentions the village Bōni (Bōni) and the mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vīra-Sāraṇadēva of Jantur-nāḍu, who was the lord of the city of Aruṇavāṭa, was born in the family of Surabhi vaṁśa and belonged to the lineage of Dūrvāsas. Mentions the Nāgakula.

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On another mutilated slab lying in Amritēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Mentions the Nāgakula.

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On the door-post of the entrance into Amritēśvara temple, right and left sides. †
cells.remarks: Gift of a lamp to the temple of Amritēśvara at Bōni by a private individual.

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On a slab lying in the middle of the village of Bhōgapuram.
cells.remarks: Records that the merchant Kannama-Nayaka constructed the Jaina temple called Rajaraja-Jinalaya at Bhōgapura and gave two puttis of land to that temple with the consent of the 11esi-Raṭṣadlu (i.e. the villagers who belonged to the mercantile class).

cells.location: Bōni †
cells.place: On another slab lying in the place of Amritēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Durgadēvi at Bhōgapura.

cells.place: On the third slab lying in the same place.
cells.remarks: Partly damaged. Gift of land measured by the jānkōla rod, below the tank of Bhōgapuram by Lōkanāthasēṭṭi, who seems to have gift of land from the Dōrākāḍu.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam
cells.place: On the third slab lying in the place of Amritēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land to the temple of Chōḍagaṅgēśvara at Dharmavaram, which was included in the Taḷḷa-nāḍu twelve, a sub-division of Puṇḍapa. The measuring rod Aṇiyārka-Bhūmikōṇi is mentioned.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam †
cells.place: On a huge stone lying in the middle of the village of Rēlivalasa.
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for lamp. Taḷḷa-nāḍu, a sub-division of Era[ḍa]-dēśa is mentioned.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam †
cells.place: On a pillar lying near a private threshing floor south-west of the same village (as Amritēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Gift of land in the village of Tēkara in Taḷḷa-nāḍu twelve, a sub-division of Eḍuḍapāṇḍu, to the temple of Chōḍagaṅga-Mādhava-dēva. The grant was made by Rachamaraṇi i.e. king's brother-in-law) Arasagoṇḍa-Rāvala in the presence of the god Timbaradēva on the bank of the Vaṁśadhārā river, for the merit of Kāmārṇavadēva. The Gaṅga capital Nahara (i.e. Mukhaliṅgam) is mentioned.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam †
cells.place: On the pillar of Amritēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for a lamp to the temple of Chōḍagaṅga-Mādhavadēva at Tuḷaḍu, by a merchant.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam
cells.place: On the pillar of Amritēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of gold for a lump to the same temple by a Nayaka Talapda is said to have been in Eradapampu.

cells.location: Dvārapuḍipāḷyam
cells.place: On the same pillar
cells.remarks: Mentions the same temple and a certain Viḍvayajñayī-Brāhma-maṇya.

cells.location: Rāmatīrtham
cells.place: On the pillar of Amritēśvara †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.location: Simhachalam
cells.place: On a round pillar in the asthana-mandapa of the Lakshminarasimhasvamin temple
cells.dynasty: Musalman †
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Narava to Nrsimha of Simhadri by the Padmanayaka Surappa-Asvarayanigaru. This chief, under orders from the Musalman king, drove beyond the boundary Mukunda-Bahinidatta. It is also stated that he granted the village of Kurumam (i.e., Srikurmam) to the temple and to the temple-servants of the deity.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On another round pillar in Lakshminarasimhasvamin temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Rayapraju, son of Chintalapati-Sambadiraju, dauntized the Kalingakapurina and had it recited with the permission of Rayananya-Sultan Pinapati-Narasimha-Gajapati-raju-Maharaju.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a third round pillar in Lakshminarasimhasvamin temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of a golden kathapra by Chatagairaya, son of Gode, presented to the temple of Varahasvamin at Simhachalam.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a round pillar in the raised veranda (tiruchuthunnal) round the central shrine of Lakshminarasimhasvamin temple. †
cells.dynasty: Vatavaya †
cells.remarks: Records that the king built a golden vessel, and presented to the temple at Simhachalam a golden aureola (prabha). He was a member of the Vatavaya family.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On another round pillar in the same veranda.
cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Anantakapalli by Jamma, son of Rava-giri, two brilliant charts and a number of cows to the lord of Simhadri, by the king, who was the son of Allada, son-in-law of Kataya-Vema and husband of Anitalli. A portion of this inscription is in the Priya chola characters, belonging to his 27th year is found at the bottom of the inscription.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: At the entrance into the Alvar shrine in Lakshminarasimhasvamin temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records gifts by a certain Prataparya.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On four faces of a pillar at the entrance into the asthana-mandapa of Alvar shrine. †
cells.remarks: Gift of five Nandasvipa for offerings in the temple of Narasimha-deva by the minister (pradhani) Saptaya for the merit of his mother Sivarani, who belonged to the Gonka family.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the south wall of Alvar shrine. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple in the same village (as Alvar shrine). †
cells.remarks: Registers certain arrangements made for celebrating a festival (in the temple) of Aḷagiyara-Perumāḷ.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the south and west walls of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Mentions the free village (taniyūr) of Kavirippakkam alias Vikrama-Sola-chaturvedimangalam in 'aduvūr-kōṭtam, a district of Jayangonda Choja-maṇdulam. Records the sale of the village of Kadaperi in Kalavaipparru of the same kōṭtam. Mentions a coin named Pirachampay kuligoi.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the west wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of land for the celebration of a festival called Sundara-Pāndyaṇsindi. Mentions Kavirippakkam in Togdai-mandalam and (the temple of) Arnjala-Perumāl at Tiruvattiyūr. The land was to be used for growing red water lilies, garlands of which had to be offered to the god on the occasion.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Damaged. The cyclic year is not distinct.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the south wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to the temple of Aḷagiya-Perumāḷ at Kavirippākkam alias Vijaya-Gaṅgai-koṇḍa-śōḷa-caturvēdimaṅgalam by Sūḷukki Nārāyaṇan Aḷavittārnāyan.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ †
cells.remarks: Sale of land. Mentions the free village (taniyūr) of Kavirippakkam alias Vikrama-Solachaturvedimangalam in Paduvūr-kōṭtum. Refers to a gift made by Mallinadaṇ Sambuvarayar.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the floor close to the south wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of gold. Mentions Ku[r]uppākkam alias Ayanāyaraṇa-caturvēdimaṅgalam.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the inner maṇdapa of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of the merit of Narsiṅgarāya-Uḍaiyar, Mon-tine the great asami[y] (vashashu) of Kavirippākkam.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions three village committees, viz. 'the great men of the annual committee,' 'the great men of the garden committee' and 'the great men of the tank committee.'

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions Muṅgaḷam, a sub-division of Paḍuvūr-kōṭṭam and Kavirippākkam (akkam alias) Amaṇinārāyaṇa-caturvēdimaṅgalam in the same koṭṭam.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On another stone built into the wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions Ka[v]irippākkam alias Ayanāyaraṇa-caturvēdimaṅgalam, the great men of the words committee. The tank committee was appointed to look after a lamp gift.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the west wall of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions the big tank (periya-ēri) and the 'tank committee'. Gift of gold.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the ceiling of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Gift of gold.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On another stone built into the same ceiling, Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On a pillar in Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Mentions (the temple called) Tiruppaḷḷippāvaram.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On another pillar in Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple †
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the third pillar in Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Simhachalam †
cells.place: On the fourth pillar in Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple. †
cells.remarks: Mentions Miḷalaikkūṟṟam in Pāṇḍināḍu.

cells.location: Kāvērippākkam
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the masjid
cells.remarks: Records the building of the masjid. At the top of this slab is an inscription in Hindustani, which is perhaps another copy of the same.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: At the foot of the entrance into the Ganga-Amman shrine in the Kottakkara temple in the same village (as Varadarāja-Perumāḷ temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions the temple of Tirumēṟṟaḷi at Kāvaḍipākkam.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Muktisvara temple in the same village (as Ganga-Amman shrine). †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Śeṅgēṇi Ammaiappaṉ [Vīramiṇḍaṉ] alias Attimallaṉ Vikrama-Chōḷa-Sambuvarāyaṉ.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: At the entrance into the gopura of Muktisvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Mutilated.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On a stone built into the bund of the tank in the same village (as Muktisvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions the temple of Tiruvakkīśvaram.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: In another stone built into the same bund, Muktisvara temple. †
cells.remarks: A fragment of the historical introduction of the king.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On a fifth stone built into the same bund, Muktisvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Mutilated.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On a fourth stone built into the same bund, Muktisvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Appears to register an endowment for offerings and for burning a perpetual lamp.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On a fifth stone built into the place of Muktisvara †
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On one of the inscribed stones kept in the Public Works Department bungalow in the same village (as Muktisvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to contain a Šaka data, the first figure of which is 3 and the second 2, while the third is lost.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On another stone in the place of Muktisvara †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions a temple called Tirunaṭṭapperumāṉaḍigaḷ and Kāvaḍippākkam.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the third stone in the place of Muktisvara †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions a Chōḷa feudatory named Parāntakappallavaraiyaṉ of Umbaḷa-nāḍu and the Chōḷa kings Jananātha and Mummaḍi-Chōḷa.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the fourth stone in the place of Muktisvara †
cells.remarks: Fragment.

cells.location: Guḍimallūr
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Bhūmīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to the temple of Kaḍāraṅgoṇḍachōḷīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyiṉār in Karaivaḷi-Valliyūr, a village of Kalavaippaṟṟu in Paḍuvūrkōṭṭam.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: The king bears Sāḷuva birudas. Mentions Kalavaippaṟṟu in Perundimiri-nāḍu, a sub-division of Paḍuvūr-kōṭṭam. Records certain arrangements made with regard to the digging of a river-channel (āṟṟukkāl). Mentions Kumāra-Krishṇappa-Nāyaka and Chinna-Bommu-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Guḍimallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Mentions the temple of Kiḍāraṅgoṇḍachōḷīśvaramuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Malliyūr.

cells.location: Guḍimallūr
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Built in. Mentions the temple of Kiḍāraṅgoṇḍachōḷēśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār at Karaivaḷi Valliyūr, a village in Kalavaippaṟṟu, a district of Paḍuvūrkōṭṭam; also the right and left hand castes.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the wall of Bhaktavatsala †
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes in favour of the Palataḷi (temple) at Kuraivāḷi-Kaḷpparu, a village in Kaḷvappāṇ.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the wall of Bhaktavatsala †
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Bommu-Nāyaka Liṅgama-Nāyakar to the weavers of Vaḷḷiyūr.

cells.place: On the wall of Bhaktavatsala †
cells.remarks: Refers to a fight between the right and left castes which lasted for four years.

cells.location: Guḍimallūr
cells.place: On the south and east walls of Bhaktavatsala temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Seems to record a gift of land.

cells.place: On the south and east walls of Bhaktavatsala temple. †
cells.remarks: Gift of land.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Records that the king remitted taxes payable both in money and in kind on lands whose crops had suffered in Kaḷvappāṇ, if such lands would not otherwise be taken up for cultivation. This order was to be engraved in the temples at Tiruvallam, Guḍimallūr (in the temple of Mannu-Nāyanār) and Kaḷvappāṇ.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Bharadvājēśvara temple near Puḍappāḍi
cells.remarks: Damaged.

cells.location: Kaverippakkam †
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Bharadvājēśvara temple near Puḍappāḍi
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the gift of a lamp to the temple of Tiruk-kuraṅgōtti-Mahādēvar in Puḍappāḍi.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Sale of land by the villagers of Puḍappāḍi in the temple of Tiruk-kuraṅgōtti in the temple of Tiruk-kuraṅgōtti-Mahādēvar. The land was situated on the north bank of the Paḷār and had become unfit for cultivation in consequence of a flood in the river, which led to the fields getting silted up with sand.

cells.location: Tiruttani — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west and south walls of Bharadvājēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Motivated. Registers a sale of land to a private individual for feeding pilgrims going to and returning from Śrīraṅgam (i.e., Upper Ganges).

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of Viraṭṭānēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Sale of land by the assembly of Jananātha-chaturvēdimangalam in Mummudi-Choḷa-nāṭu (a district) of Jayangoṇḍa-Choḷamaṇḍalam to a private individual for feeding pilgrims going to and returning from Śrīraṅgam.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of Viraṭṭānēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of 12 sheep for a lamp to burn at (the temple of) Tiruviratṭānam Udaiyar.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of Viraṭṭānēśvara †

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu

cells.remarks: Records that a certain Nambi-Appi built the temple at Tirattaniyal of granite. The verse (venbā) is said to have been composed by the king, whose name is, however, not given. (Marayali)

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of Viraṭṭānēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 30 cows for a lamp. The temple is called Tiruviraṭṭānam-uḍaiya-Mahādēvar in Tiruttaniyāl.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of Viraṭṭānēśvara †
cells.remarks: Gift of 1,000 kuli of land by Nambi-Appi to the temple of Tiravittai.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the east wall of the mandapa in front of Viraṭṭānēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of Viraṭṭānēśvara †

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu

cells.remarks: Built in, at the bottom. Gift of isid apparently by a certain Parakēsari Muttaraiyay to the temple of Subrahmayappillaiyar, who was pleased to stand on the hill at Tiruttaniyal (near) Agnuvūr, the eastern hamlet of Perungāṇiji in Ogavala-nādu (a district of) Melur-kōṭṭam, which formed part of Jayaṅgonda Chola-mandalam. The character of the inscription are comparatively modern.

cells.location: Tiruttani † — Tamil Nadu

Sale of the village of Medavur in Naduvinmalai-Perumur-nādu.

cells.location: Tiruvālaṅgāḍu

Nos. 460 and 461 are engraved in comparatively modern characters of about the 12th century. They may be copies of old inscriptions, though no statement to that effect is made.

cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāra of the Naṭarājasvāmin shrine in the Vaidyanāthasvāmi temple
cells.remarks: Gift of the proceeds of certain taxes to the temple at Tiruvālaṅgāḍu by Tikkamāṇi for maintaining perpetual lamps. The document is signed by Tikkamāṇi.

cells.location: Tiruvālaṅgāḍu

cells.remarks: Sale of land by the assembly of Peruṅkūr alias Rājānārāyaṇa-chaturvēdimangalam in Peruṅkūr-nāḍu.
